extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, corporate communicators, press-release writers, marketing teams
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing the short 'About [Company]' boilerplate at the end of a press release: its purpose, tone, length/format, required content, placement, and maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A boilerplate briefly describes the firm in a professional tone, highlighting key information so a reader can quickly grasp what the firm is, does, and where to get more details. It's the company's elevator pitch in written form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the boilerplate as a concise company summary that orients journalists/readers; avoid long history or narrative. Keep it professional and informational rather than promotional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideal length: 50-100 words; single paragraph; roughly 2-3 sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the boilerplate compact — aim for the 50-100 word sweet spot. Present as a single paragraph to match common press-release formatting and to be easily copy/pasted into media materials. 2–3 sentences typically suffice to cover the essentials without extraneous detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Lean formal; use third person; factual, not promotional (avoid claims like 'the best,' 'the greatest,' 'the only').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write objectively and avoid marketing superlatives. Use third-person phrasing (e.g., 'Company X is...') so the boilerplate reads like an informational summary a journalist can reuse. Avoid puffery and overt sales language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key content: clear statement of what the company does
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a clear, concise statement of what the company does.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with a short description of the company’s primary business, product, or service so readers instantly understand the firm's core function or market. Avoid vague or fluffy descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key content: one credibility item
rubrics_metrics.description: Include one impressive statistic, award, or unique positioning for credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a single supporting fact that lends credibility (e.g., a notable award, user count, market share, years in business, or unique positioning). Keep this to one, impactful item to avoid clutter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key content: geographic/market position
rubrics_metrics.description: State where you operate or your market position (if relevant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If location or market coverage is relevant to the release, succinctly note headquarters, primary markets, or geographic reach. Only include if it adds meaningful context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key content: end with website URL
rubrics_metrics.description: Always end the boilerplate with the website URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a direct URL at the end so readers and journalists can easily find more information. Make sure the URL is current and correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid buzzwords (e.g., 'innovative,' 'world-class,' 'cutting-edge'); avoid repeating information from other sections of the release; avoid marketing-speak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not recycle promotional language from the headline or body; instead use factual, distinct boilerplate content. Steer clear of cliché buzzwords and generic adjectives that add no informational value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Place the boilerplate at the end of the press release, before contact info, headed 'About [Company]'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard placement aids journalists and readers in finding company background quickly. Use the conventional 'About [Company]' heading so it's immediately recognizable and separate from the news content and contact details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep boilerplate up-to-date; update with new awards, product lines, milestones; review at least annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a cadence (at least yearly) to refresh the boilerplate so it reflects the company's current size, offerings, achievements, and web address. Update sooner when there are significant changes (new flagship product, major award, rebranding).
